title: A noob learns FFT
excerpt: I have never done any time–frequency transformations. I understand the general idea, but I have never worked with the details. Today I had a reason to use it, but that means learning the basics first.
content_html:
I have never done any time–frequency transformations. I understand the general idea, but I have never worked with the details. Today I had a reason to use it, but that means learning the basics first.

Pure sine wave

The following is three seconds of a single 5 Hz sine wave, recorded at a sample rate of 100 Hz.1 Well, it’s synthetically generated, but that’s what it represents.

If we run this through the fft function in R, we get a bunch of complex numbers – as many as we have samples. In this case, that’s 300 of them. The values of these numbers depend on the amplitude of the signal, so for this signal, they should max out at 1. However, coming out of the R fft function, these values are also scaled up by the number of samples. In the following plot, I have divided by the number of samples to get the amplitudes back out.

Each point corresponds to the signal amplitude at a specific frequency. Of the 300 points in that plot, 298 of them sit at the origin, because there is no signal with their frequency in the data.

The two points that do exist away from the origin makes it seem like our data had two frequencies, but we only had one! I have to admit this is a quirk of the Fourier transform I don’t fully understand, but apparently the transformation looks at our 5 Hz signal with amplitude 1 and sees two signals:

  • One 5 Hz signal with amplitude 0.5, and
  • One −5 Hz signal with amplitude −0.5.

These add up to a single 5 Hz signal of amplitude 1. Or something.

Anyway, in this latest plot, the X axis (the real part of the numbers that come out of fft) correspond to the cosine signal at that point, whereas the Y axis (the imaginary part) correspond to the sine signal at that point. Since we only had a sine wave, the real part is zero for all frequencies.

However, that is a bit of a misleading way to look at it. The reason each frequency output is a complex number is because a sine plus a cosine lets us represent a wave of any phase. So it’s more intuitive to look at these complex numbers through their magnitude and angle. The angle is the least interesting. We’ll start with that.

As we have said, the output of fft is a vector of the same length as the original data. Each value in this vector corresponds to a frequency, with the first value being “frequency zero”, or the mean of the data. The values after that correspond to frequencies that are linearly spaced out so that the last frequency is just below the sampling rate. In the following plot, I have transformed the X axis from vector indices to frequencies accordingly. The highest frequency in the plot is nearly the sampling rate of 100 per second.

The phase goes from \(-\pi\) to \(\pi\), and in our case it is all over the place. But that’s not surprising! We don’t have any signal at most of these frequencies, so we don’t care what the phase is there. What we care about is the amplitude of the signal at each frequency, and that has the shape we expect. Here we plot the magnitude of the complex numbers in the fft output, rather than their angle.

These two bars correspond to 5 Hz and −5 Hz. We can simplify this plot by adding up the mirrored amplitudes and only plotting the first half of the spectrum. After all, Nyquist suggests we cannot recover signals with a frequency higher than half the sample rate.

There we go! We recovered the full amplitude of the 5 Hz pure sine wave signal we had. Already there were a lot more details to account for than I knew.

Truncated signal

In the above case, we presented an unnaturally clean signal. The data was even constructed so the sample window captured a whole number of cycles. If we cut the sample off prematurely, we get spectral leakage.

Here are the raw complex values from the fft of the same signal, except we stopped recording at 2.9 seconds, instead of 3 seconds.

This looks nothing like the previous result. It’s a bit easier to see what happened when we look at the amplitudes at various frequencies.

Truncation causes spectral leakage that smears out the clean 5 Hz sine wave into a group of closely related signals. Practically speaking, it’s no big deal: we can still perfectly reconstruct the original signal. The leakage only makes the spectrum look confusing, it doesn’t actually destroy any data.

A common way to deal with truncation is to apply an envelope function to the data that smoothly transitions it to zero near the endpoints. The below plots show the exact same signal as before, except attenuated toward the ends.

This envelope adds some fuzziness to the spectrum, but it does effectively get rid of the spectral leakage.

A noisy, composite signal

If we add a little noise to the signal, the fft still gets a representative spectrum out of it.

We can see the peak around 5 Hz, but with a noise floor at all other frequencies. In the next group of plots, I have added another sine wave to the signal. It’s hard to tell with this level of noise, but thanks to the magic of the Fourier transform, I’m sure you can pick the frequency out.

Yep, the 5 Hz wave is still there, and now we also have a 23 Hz wave.

Odd signals

Here are some odd signal types that we might want to know what they look like in the frequency domain. First up, an impulse.

Although it’s not really visible here, the impulse has raised the floor of the spectrum – it contributes to all frequencies.

By contrast, a step function contributes in a decaying manner to low frequencies.

A square wave contributes with decaying odd harmonics.

An autoregressive/decaying impulse looks similar to the step function, but smoother.

But enough playing around. There’s some real data I’m interested in.

Computing real growth

I can’t say what this data really means, but fortunately I have a corny cover story ready: outside my children’s bedroom, they’re constructing a building. We’ll pretend I have a measuring device that records the increase in building height every hour, and it’s been doing that for a year.

Because the construction workers primarily work during the day, and on weekdays, I expect daily cycles (building growth from day to day), and weekly cycles (lulls in growth during weekends). In the plot below, the frequency spectrum has been changed to a period spectrum. Thus, a peak at 7 in the spectrum corresponds to a weekly cycle, rather than a frequency of 7 per day.

The tallest bar in the spectrum corresponds to a cycle with a period of 365 days. Obviously, given just one year of data, we cannot know whether this is a repeating cycle or not; the bar really only represents a general increase toward the end of the year, and that’s probably true: it seems that building growth has increased.

Aside from the one-day and seven-day cycles we expected, there is also a prominent cycle with a period of 3.5 days. This shows up because the weekday pattern is really a square wave with a duty cycle of 5-on, 2-off. The harmonics we expect to be prominent for that square wave are cycles of length 3.5 days, 2.4 days, 1.4 days, and 1.2 days. There are peaks corresponding to all of those cycles in the spectrum!

Although it’s not visible on this small plot, the spectrum also contains a cycle with a period of two hours. It would be interesting to see if there’s an hourly cycle, but the Nyquist limit says the shortest cycle we can extract from hourly data is one with a period of two hours.

But if we look up from the spectrum onto the time series, we see some sharp peaks in the data. Those are not, generally, real growth. To roll with our corny example, we can pretend that these are artifacts of someone bumping into the table which holds the measuring device, causing a false signal. I want to see what the real growth is over the year, so I need to somehow subtract the bumps from the signal.

Thinking back to our earlier experimentation, we may realise that the bumps are impulses! Maybe we can assume they contribute equally to all frequencies. Then we ought to be able to subtract a constant magnitude from all frequencies and get rid of the worst of the table bumps. I didn’t expect it to work, but it kind of does.

Looking at the filtered time series at the top, the weekly cycles become so much more apparent after filtering out the worst of the false signals. It seems increasingly like there’s one specific day of the week where they do most of the actual construction of the building.2 I notice that my cover story is starting to break apart. Please suspend your disbelief.

We can tell from the period spectrum that the filtering operation had the practical effect of attenuating much of the high-frequency noise, i.e. that with periods shorter than one day. The result is somewhat similar to a rolling median, but the fft based approach retains the day-to-day variation better. For the rolling median have sufficient bump-filtering strength, it must have a window size that is also large enough that it also smooths out much of the daily cycle.

If we think of the peaks as a high-frequency component instead of as separate impulses, we would instead attempt to filter them out with a low-pass filter. This would also zero out the short-period components of the spectrum, but it wouldn’t have any effect on the long-period components. I tried this also, but it didn’t work as well.

I suspct the reason we can’t think of the peaks as high-frequency components is that they are somewhat randomly dispersed. They don’t make up one unified high-frequency signal. Maybe if we made a spectrum for a zoomed-in part of the time series, we could think of them as high-frequency components. Let’s formalise that idea a bit.

Making a spectrogram

In the above analysis we produced a single spectrum for the full year of hourly growth. We could imagine cutting the year up into smaller chunks and computing the spectrum for each chunk. The benefit of this is that if the spectrum changes over the year, we’d get custom spectrums for each chunk, rather than one that’s too general to do anything with.

It’s not obvious what size chunks we should select. Smaller chunks allow us to react to smaller changes in the spectrum, but on the other hand, the length of the chunk sets a limit on the length of the cycle we can detect. Here are some alternatives:

  • We can reject daily chunks right away, because there is practically only noise in the signal moving faster than daily cycles.
  • We could try weekly chunks, since that would allow us to spot both the daily cycles and weekly cycles. However, having tried weekly chunks, in practice the fft gets too little data per chunk to actually extract any meaningful cycles at all.
  • Biweekly chunks had similar problems as weekly chunks.
  • Monthly chunks are a bit noisy, but work okay.
  • Quarterly chunks also work, but the first three quarters are wholly uninteresting.

What we get out of this is called a spectrogram. The below uses monthly chunks, but regardless of chunk size, the nice thing about plotting the spectrogram under the time series is that we can immediately spot the relationship.

The columns of the spectrogram that are darker correspond to regions of the time series with less activity. The bright columns have more activity. That much is immediately clear!

Then looking more carefully, the weekly cycle is actually not visible during the first 200 or so days of the year. The daily cycle is faint, but visible in almost all months. In the third-to-last month, the weekly cycle seems to be replaced with a biweekly cycle! The overtones of the weekly cycle are really prominent in the last two months.

The drawback of making the spectrogram like this is that if useful information straddles a monthly boundary, the spectrum for either of the months may not catch it. We can address this by sliding a window across the time series instead. The plot below is still made with a monthly window, except instead of jumping from one month to the next, it slides 12 hours over at a time.

I’m not yet sure I understand all the patterns that come up, but it’s fun to look at and think about!

But now, maybe now we can think of the peaks as high-frequency components? We’d take the spectrum for each window, toss it through a low-pass filter, and then reconstruct the original time series from those consecutive spectra. Thrilling stuff! But that sounds a bit tedious to write the code for, I’ve already spent too long on this article, and there’s another idea I want to explore first.

This marks the end of my fft experiments for now. I’ve definitely become a lot more comfortable with it, and now consider it a tool in my toolkit I didn’t have before. Thanks for tagging along for the ride!

In the following plot, I have transformed the X axis from vector indices to frequencies accordingly. The highest frequency in the plot is nearly the sampling rate of 100 per second.

sentences.en: As we have said, the output of fft is a vector of the same length as the original data.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，fft的输出是与原始数据长度相同的向量。

sentences.en: Each value in this vector corresponds to a frequency, with the first value being “frequency zero”, or the mean of the data.
sentences.zh: 该向量中的每个值对应于一个频率，第一个值是“频率零”，或数据的平均值。

sentences.en: The values after that correspond to frequencies that are linearly spaced out so that the last frequency is just below the sampling rate.
sentences.zh: 之后的值对应于线性间隔的频率，因此最后一个频率略低于采样率。

sentences.en: In the following plot, I have transformed the X axis from vector indices to frequencies accordingly.
sentences.zh: 在下图中，我已将 X 轴相应地从矢量索引转换为频率。

sentences.en: The highest frequency in the plot is nearly the sampling rate of 100 per second.
sentences.zh: 图中的最高频率接近每秒 100 次的采样率。

blocks.html_en: The phase goes from \(-\pi\) to \(\pi\), and in our case it is all over the place. But that’s not surprising! We don’t have any signal at most of these frequencies, so we don’t care what the phase is there. What we care about is the amplitude of the signal at each frequency, and that has the shape we expect. Here we plot the magnitude of the complex numbers in the fft output, rather than their angle.

sentences.en: The phase goes from \(-\pi\) to \(\pi\), and in our case it is all over the place.
sentences.zh: 相位从 \(-\pi\) 到 \(\pi\)，在我们的例子中，它无处不在。

sentences.en: But that’s not surprising!
sentences.zh: 但这并不奇怪！

sentences.en: We don’t have any signal at most of these frequencies, so we don’t care what the phase is there.
sentences.zh: 在大多数这些频率下我们没有任何信号，所以我们不关心相位是多少。

sentences.en: What we care about is the amplitude of the signal at each frequency, and that has the shape we expect.
sentences.zh: 我们关心的是每个频率下信号的幅度，它具有我们期望的形状。

sentences.en: Here we plot the magnitude of the complex numbers in the fft output, rather than their angle.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们绘制 fft 输出中复数的大小，而不是它们的角度。

blocks.html_en: These two bars correspond to 5 Hz and −5 Hz. We can simplify this plot by adding up the mirrored amplitudes and only plotting the first half of the spectrum. After all, Nyquist suggests we cannot recover signals with a frequency higher than half the sample rate.

sentences.en: These two bars correspond to 5 Hz and −5 Hz.
sentences.zh: 这两个条对应于 5 Hz 和 −5 Hz。

sentences.en: We can simplify this plot by adding up the mirrored amplitudes and only plotting the first half of the spectrum.
sentences.zh: 我们可以通过将镜像幅度相加并仅绘制频谱的前半部分来简化该图。

sentences.en: After all, Nyquist suggests we cannot recover signals with a frequency higher than half the sample rate.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，奈奎斯特表明我们无法恢复频率高于采样率一半的信号。

blocks.html_en: There we go! We recovered the full amplitude of the 5 Hz pure sine wave signal we had. Already there were a lot more details to account for than I knew.

sentences.en: There we go!
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧！

sentences.en: We recovered the full amplitude of the 5 Hz pure sine wave signal we had.
sentences.zh: 我们恢复了 5 Hz 纯正弦波信号的全振幅。

sentences.en: Already there were a lot more details to account for than I knew.
sentences.zh: 已经有比我知道的更多的细节需要解释了。

blocks.html_en: Truncated signal

sentences.en: Truncated signal
sentences.zh: 截断信号

blocks.html_en: In the above case, we presented an unnaturally clean signal. The data was even constructed so the sample window captured a whole number of cycles. If we cut the sample off prematurely, we get spectral leakage.

sentences.en: In the above case, we presented an unnaturally clean signal.
sentences.zh: 在上述情况下，我们呈现了一个不自然的干净信号。

sentences.en: The data was even constructed so the sample window captured a whole number of cycles.
sentences.zh: 数据甚至被构建为样本窗口捕获了整数个周期。

sentences.en: If we cut the sample off prematurely, we get spectral leakage.
sentences.zh: 如果我们过早地切断样本，就会出现光谱泄漏。

blocks.html_en: Here are the raw complex values from the fft of the same signal, except we stopped recording at 2.9 seconds, instead of 3 seconds.

sentences.en: Here are the raw complex values from the fft of the same signal, except we stopped recording at 2.9 seconds, instead of 3 seconds.
sentences.zh: 以下是同一信号的 fft 的原始复数值，只不过我们在 2.9 秒而不是 3 秒处停止记录。

blocks.html_en: This looks nothing like the previous result. It’s a bit easier to see what happened when we look at the amplitudes at various frequencies.

sentences.en: This looks nothing like the previous result.
sentences.zh: 这看起来与之前的结果完全不同。

sentences.en: It’s a bit easier to see what happened when we look at the amplitudes at various frequencies.
sentences.zh: 当我们观察不同频率下的振幅时，更容易看出发生了什么。

blocks.html_en: Truncation causes spectral leakage that smears out the clean 5 Hz sine wave into a group of closely related signals. Practically speaking, it’s no big deal: we can still perfectly reconstruct the original signal. The leakage only makes the spectrum look confusing, it doesn’t actually destroy any data.

sentences.en: Truncation causes spectral leakage that smears out the clean 5 Hz sine wave into a group of closely related signals.
sentences.zh: 截断会导致频谱泄漏，将干净的 5 Hz 正弦波涂抹成一组密切相关的信号。

sentences.en: Practically speaking, it’s no big deal: we can still perfectly reconstruct the original signal.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这没什么大不了的：我们仍然可以完美地重建原始信号。

sentences.en: The leakage only makes the spectrum look confusing, it doesn’t actually destroy any data.
sentences.zh: 泄漏只会使频谱看起来混乱，实际上并不会破坏任何数据。

blocks.html_en: A common way to deal with truncation is to apply an envelope function to the data that smoothly transitions it to zero near the endpoints. The below plots show the exact same signal as before, except attenuated toward the ends.

sentences.en: A common way to deal with truncation is to apply an envelope function to the data that smoothly transitions it to zero near the endpoints.
sentences.zh: 处理截断的常见方法是对数据应用包络函数，将其平滑地过渡到端点附近的零。

sentences.en: The below plots show the exact same signal as before, except attenuated toward the ends.
sentences.zh: 下图显示了与之前完全相同的信号，除了向末端衰减之外。

blocks.html_en: This envelope adds some fuzziness to the spectrum, but it does effectively get rid of the spectral leakage.

sentences.en: This envelope adds some fuzziness to the spectrum, but it does effectively get rid of the spectral leakage.
sentences.zh: 该包络给频谱增加了一些模糊性，但它确实有效地消除了频谱泄漏。

blocks.html_en: A noisy, composite signal

sentences.en: A noisy, composite signal
sentences.zh: 嘈杂的复合信号

blocks.html_en: If we add a little noise to the signal, the fft still gets a representative spectrum out of it.

sentences.en: If we add a little noise to the signal, the fft still gets a representative spectrum out of it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们向信号添加一点噪声，快速傅立叶变换仍然可以从中获得代表性频谱。

blocks.html_en: We can see the peak around 5 Hz, but with a noise floor at all other frequencies. In the next group of plots, I have added another sine wave to the signal. It’s hard to tell with this level of noise, but thanks to the magic of the Fourier transform, I’m sure you can pick the frequency out.

sentences.en: We can see the peak around 5 Hz, but with a noise floor at all other frequencies.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到 5 Hz 左右的峰值，但在所有其他频率处都有本底噪声。

sentences.en: In the next group of plots, I have added another sine wave to the signal.
sentences.zh: 在下一组图中，我向信号添加了另一个正弦波。

sentences.en: It’s hard to tell with this level of noise, but thanks to the magic of the Fourier transform, I’m sure you can pick the frequency out.
sentences.zh: 在这种水平的噪音下很难分辨，但由于傅里叶变换的魔力，我相信你可以选出频率。

blocks.html_en: Yep, the 5 Hz wave is still there, and now we also have a 23 Hz wave.

sentences.en: Yep, the 5 Hz wave is still there, and now we also have a 23 Hz wave.
sentences.zh: 是的，5 Hz 波仍然存在，现在我们还有 23 Hz 波。

blocks.html_en: Odd signals

sentences.en: Odd signals
sentences.zh: 奇数信号

blocks.html_en: Here are some odd signal types that we might want to know what they look like in the frequency domain. First up, an impulse.

sentences.en: Here are some odd signal types that we might want to know what they look like in the frequency domain.
sentences.zh: 以下是一些奇怪的信号类型，我们可能想知道它们在频域中的样子。

sentences.en: First up, an impulse.
sentences.zh: 首先，是一种冲动。

blocks.html_en: Although it’s not really visible here, the impulse has raised the floor of the spectrum – it contributes to all frequencies.

sentences.en: Although it’s not really visible here, the impulse has raised the floor of the spectrum – it contributes to all frequencies.
sentences.zh: 虽然在这里并不真正可见，但脉冲提高了频谱的下限——它对所有频率都有贡献。

blocks.html_en: By contrast, a step function contributes in a decaying manner to low frequencies.

sentences.en: By contrast, a step function contributes in a decaying manner to low frequencies.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，阶跃函数以衰减的方式对低频产生影响。

blocks.html_en: A square wave contributes with decaying odd harmonics.

sentences.en: A square wave contributes with decaying odd harmonics.
sentences.zh: 方波有助于衰减奇次谐波。

blocks.html_en: An autoregressive/decaying impulse looks similar to the step function, but smoother.

sentences.en: An autoregressive/decaying impulse looks similar to the step function, but smoother.
sentences.zh: 自回归/衰减脉冲看起来与阶跃函数类似，但更平滑。

blocks.html_en: But enough playing around. There’s some real data I’m interested in.

sentences.en: But enough playing around.
sentences.zh: 但玩够了。

sentences.en: There’s some real data I’m interested in.
sentences.zh: 有一些我感兴趣的真实数据。

blocks.html_en: Computing real growth

sentences.en: Computing real growth
sentences.zh: 计算实际增长

blocks.html_en: I can’t say what this data really means, but fortunately I have a corny cover story ready: outside my children’s bedroom, they’re constructing a building. We’ll pretend I have a measuring device that records the increase in building height every hour, and it’s been doing that for a year.

sentences.en: I can’t say what this data really means, but fortunately I have a corny cover story ready: outside my children’s bedroom, they’re constructing a building.
sentences.zh: 我无法说出这些数据的真正含义，但幸运的是，我已经准备好了一个陈词滥调的封面故事：在我孩子们的卧室外面，他们正在建造一座建筑物。

sentences.en: We’ll pretend I have a measuring device that records the increase in building height every hour, and it’s been doing that for a year.
sentences.zh: 我们假设我有一个测量设备，可以记录每小时建筑物高度的增加，并且它已经这样做了一年。

blocks.html_en: Because the construction workers primarily work during the day, and on weekdays, I expect daily cycles (building growth from day to day), and weekly cycles (lulls in growth during weekends). In the plot below, the frequency spectrum has been changed to a period spectrum. Thus, a peak at 7 in the spectrum corresponds to a weekly cycle, rather than a frequency of 7 per day.

sentences.en: Because the construction workers primarily work during the day, and on weekdays, I expect daily cycles (building growth from day to day), and weekly cycles (lulls in growth during weekends).
sentences.zh: 因为建筑工人主要在白天和工作日工作，所以我预计会有每日周期（建筑日复一日地增长）和每周周期（周末增长停滞）。

sentences.en: In the plot below, the frequency spectrum has been changed to a period spectrum.
sentences.zh: 在下图中，频谱已更改为周期频谱。

sentences.en: Thus, a peak at 7 in the spectrum corresponds to a weekly cycle, rather than a frequency of 7 per day.
sentences.zh: 因此，频谱中 7 处的峰值对应于每周周期，而不是每天 7 的频率。

blocks.html_en: The tallest bar in the spectrum corresponds to a cycle with a period of 365 days. Obviously, given just one year of data, we cannot know whether this is a repeating cycle or not; the bar really only represents a general increase toward the end of the year, and that’s probably true: it seems that building growth has increased.

sentences.en: The tallest bar in the spectrum corresponds to a cycle with a period of 365 days.
sentences.zh: 频谱中最高的条对应于 365 天的周期。

sentences.en: Obviously, given just one year of data, we cannot know whether this is a repeating cycle or not; the bar really only represents a general increase toward the end of the year, and that’s probably true: it seems that building growth has increased.
sentences.zh: 显然，仅仅给出一年的数据，我们无法知道这是否是一个重复的周期；该条实际上仅代表接近年底的总体增长，这可能是正确的：建筑增长似乎有所增加。

blocks.html_en: Aside from the one-day and seven-day cycles we expected, there is also a prominent cycle with a period of 3.5 days. This shows up because the weekday pattern is really a square wave with a duty cycle of 5-on, 2-off. The harmonics we expect to be prominent for that square wave are cycles of length 3.5 days, 2.4 days, 1.4 days, and 1.2 days. There are peaks corresponding to all of those cycles in the spectrum!

sentences.en: Aside from the one-day and seven-day cycles we expected, there is also a prominent cycle with a period of 3.5 days.
sentences.zh: 除了我们预期的1天和7天周期外，还有一个突出的周期是3.5天。

sentences.en: This shows up because the weekday pattern is really a square wave with a duty cycle of 5-on, 2-off.
sentences.zh: 出现这种情况是因为工作日模式实际上是一个占空比为 5 开、2 关的方波。

sentences.en: The harmonics we expect to be prominent for that square wave are cycles of length 3.5 days, 2.4 days, 1.4 days, and 1.2 days.
sentences.zh: 我们预计该方波的主要谐波是长度为 3.5 天、2.4 天、1.4 天和 1.2 天的周期。

sentences.en: There are peaks corresponding to all of those cycles in the spectrum!
sentences.zh: 光谱中的所有这些周期都有对应的峰值！

blocks.html_en: Although it’s not visible on this small plot, the spectrum also contains a cycle with a period of two hours. It would be interesting to see if there’s an hourly cycle, but the Nyquist limit says the shortest cycle we can extract from hourly data is one with a period of two hours.

sentences.en: Although it’s not visible on this small plot, the spectrum also contains a cycle with a period of two hours.
sentences.zh: 虽然在这个小图上看不到，但光谱也包含一个周期为两个小时的周期。

sentences.en: It would be interesting to see if there’s an hourly cycle, but the Nyquist limit says the shortest cycle we can extract from hourly data is one with a period of two hours.
sentences.zh: 看看是否存在每小时周期会很有趣，但奈奎斯特极限表明我们可以从每小时数据中提取的最短周期是一个周期为两小时的周期。

blocks.html_en: But if we look up from the spectrum onto the time series, we see some sharp peaks in the data. Those are not, generally, real growth. To roll with our corny example, we can pretend that these are artifacts of someone bumping into the table which holds the measuring device, causing a false signal. I want to see what the real growth is over the year, so I need to somehow subtract the bumps from the signal.

sentences.en: But if we look up from the spectrum onto the time series, we see some sharp peaks in the data.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们从频谱中查找时间序列，我们会在数据中看到一些尖锐的峰值。

sentences.en: Those are not, generally, real growth.
sentences.zh: 一般来说，这些都不是真正的增长。

sentences.en: To roll with our corny example, we can pretend that these are artifacts of someone bumping into the table which holds the measuring device, causing a false signal.
sentences.zh: 举个老生常谈的例子，我们可以假装这些是有人撞到装有测量设备的桌子上造成的假象，从而导致了错误信号。

sentences.en: I want to see what the real growth is over the year, so I need to somehow subtract the bumps from the signal.
sentences.zh: 我想了解一年中的实际增长情况，因此我需要以某种方式从信号中减去颠簸。

blocks.html_en: Thinking back to our earlier experimentation, we may realise that the bumps are impulses! Maybe we can assume they contribute equally to all frequencies. Then we ought to be able to subtract a constant magnitude from all frequencies and get rid of the worst of the table bumps. I didn’t expect it to work, but it kind of does.

sentences.en: Thinking back to our earlier experimentation, we may realise that the bumps are impulses!
sentences.zh: 回想一下我们之前的实验，我们可能会意识到颠簸是冲动！

sentences.en: Maybe we can assume they contribute equally to all frequencies.
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以假设它们对所有频率的贡献相同。

sentences.en: Then we ought to be able to subtract a constant magnitude from all frequencies and get rid of the worst of the table bumps.
sentences.zh: 然后我们应该能够从所有频率中减去恒定的幅度并消除最严重的表颠簸。

sentences.en: I didn’t expect it to work, but it kind of does.
sentences.zh: 我没想到它会起作用，但它确实起作用了。

blocks.html_en: Looking at the filtered time series at the top, the weekly cycles become so much more apparent after filtering out the worst of the false signals. It seems increasingly like there’s one specific day of the week where they do most of the actual construction of the building.2 I notice that my cover story is starting to break apart. Please suspend your disbelief.

sentences.en: Looking at the filtered time series at the top, the weekly cycles become so much more apparent after filtering out the worst of the false signals.
sentences.zh: 看看顶部过滤后的时间序列，在过滤掉最糟糕的错误信号后，每周的周期变得更加明显。

sentences.en: It seems increasingly like there’s one specific day of the week where they do most of the actual construction of the building.22 I notice that my cover story is starting to break apart.
sentences.zh: 看起来越来越像一周中的某一天，他们负责建筑物的大部分实际施工。22我注意到我的掩盖故事开始破裂。

sentences.en: Please suspend your disbelief.
sentences.zh: 请暂停你的怀疑。

blocks.html_en: We can tell from the period spectrum that the filtering operation had the practical effect of attenuating much of the high-frequency noise, i.e. that with periods shorter than one day. The result is somewhat similar to a rolling median, but the fft based approach retains the day-to-day variation better. For the rolling median have sufficient bump-filtering strength, it must have a window size that is also large enough that it also smooths out much of the daily cycle.

sentences.en: We can tell from the period spectrum that the filtering operation had the practical effect of attenuating much of the high-frequency noise, i.e. that with periods shorter than one day.
sentences.zh: 从周期谱中我们可以看出，滤波操作具有衰减大部分高频噪声（即周期短于一天的噪声）的实际效果。

sentences.en: The result is somewhat similar to a rolling median, but the fft based approach retains the day-to-day variation better.
sentences.zh: 结果有点类似于滚动中位数，但基于 fft 的方法更好地保留了日常变化。

sentences.en: For the rolling median have sufficient bump-filtering strength, it must have a window size that is also large enough that it also smooths out much of the daily cycle.
sentences.zh: 为了使滚动中值具有足够的凹凸过滤强度，它必须具有足够大的窗口大小，以便能够平滑大部分日常周期。

blocks.html_en: If we think of the peaks as a high-frequency component instead of as separate impulses, we would instead attempt to filter them out with a low-pass filter. This would also zero out the short-period components of the spectrum, but it wouldn’t have any effect on the long-period components. I tried this also, but it didn’t work as well.

sentences.en: If we think of the peaks as a high-frequency component instead of as separate impulses, we would instead attempt to filter them out with a low-pass filter.
sentences.zh: 如果我们将峰值视为高频分量而不是单独的脉冲，我们会尝试使用低通滤波器将其滤除。

sentences.en: This would also zero out the short-period components of the spectrum, but it wouldn’t have any effect on the long-period components.
sentences.zh: 这也会将频谱的短周期分量清零，但不会对长周期分量产生任何影响。

sentences.en: I tried this also, but it didn’t work as well.
sentences.zh: 我也尝试过这个，但效果并不好。

blocks.html_en: I suspct the reason we can’t think of the peaks as high-frequency components is that they are somewhat randomly dispersed. They don’t make up one unified high-frequency signal. Maybe if we made a spectrum for a zoomed-in part of the time series, we could think of them as high-frequency components. Let’s formalise that idea a bit.

sentences.en: I suspct the reason we can’t think of the peaks as high-frequency components is that they are somewhat randomly dispersed.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑我们不能将峰值视为高频分量的原因是它们在某种程度上是随机分散的。

sentences.en: They don’t make up one unified high-frequency signal.
sentences.zh: 它们并不构成一个统一的高频信号。

sentences.en: Maybe if we made a spectrum for a zoomed-in part of the time series, we could think of them as high-frequency components.
sentences.zh: 也许如果我们为时间序列的放大部分制作频谱，我们可以将它们视为高频分量。

sentences.en: Let’s formalise that idea a bit.
sentences.zh: 让我们稍微形式化一下这个想法。

blocks.html_en: Making a spectrogram

sentences.en: Making a spectrogram
sentences.zh: 制作频谱图

blocks.html_en: In the above analysis we produced a single spectrum for the full year of hourly growth. We could imagine cutting the year up into smaller chunks and computing the spectrum for each chunk. The benefit of this is that if the spectrum changes over the year, we’d get custom spectrums for each chunk, rather than one that’s too general to do anything with.

sentences.en: In the above analysis we produced a single spectrum for the full year of hourly growth.
sentences.zh: 在上述分析中，我们生成了全年每小时增长的单一频谱。

sentences.en: We could imagine cutting the year up into smaller chunks and computing the spectrum for each chunk.
sentences.zh: 我们可以想象将一年分成更小的块并计算每个块的频谱。

sentences.en: The benefit of this is that if the spectrum changes over the year, we’d get custom spectrums for each chunk, rather than one that’s too general to do anything with.
sentences.zh: 这样做的好处是，如果频谱在一年中发生变化，我们将为每个块获得自定义频谱，而不是过于笼统而无法执行任何操作的频谱。

blocks.html_en: It’s not obvious what size chunks we should select. Smaller chunks allow us to react to smaller changes in the spectrum, but on the other hand, the length of the chunk sets a limit on the length of the cycle we can detect. Here are some alternatives:

sentences.en: It’s not obvious what size chunks we should select.
sentences.zh: 我们应该选择多大的块并不明显。

sentences.en: Smaller chunks allow us to react to smaller changes in the spectrum, but on the other hand, the length of the chunk sets a limit on the length of the cycle we can detect.
sentences.zh: 较小的块允许我们对频谱中较小的变化做出反应，但另一方面，块的长度对我们可以检测到的周期的长度设置了限制。

sentences.en: Here are some alternatives:
sentences.zh: 以下是一些替代方案：

blocks.html_en: • We can reject daily chunks right away, because there is practically only noise in the signal moving faster than daily cycles.

我从来没有做过任何时频变换。 我了解总体思路，但我从未研究过细节。 今天我有一个使用它的理由，但这意味着首先学习基础知识。

纯正弦波

下面是一个 5 Hz 正弦波的三秒，以 100 Hz 的采样率记录。11 好吧，它是合成生成的，但这就是它所代表的意思。

如果我们通过 R 中的 fft 函数运行它，我们会得到一堆复数——与我们有样本一样多。 在本例中，即 300 个。 这些数字的值取决于信号的幅度，因此对于该信号，它们的最大值应为 1。 然而，从 R fft 函数中得出，这些值也会按样本数量按比例放大。 在下图中，我除以样本数以获得幅度。

每个点对应于特定频率下的信号幅度。 该图中的 300 个点中，有 298 个位于原点，因为数据中没有包含其频率的信号。

远离原点确实存在的两个点使得我们的数据看起来有两个频率，但我们只有一个！ 我必须承认这是我不完全理解的傅立叶变换的一个怪癖，但显然该变换查看幅度为 1 的 5 Hz 信号并看到两个信号：

  • 一个幅度为 0.5 的 5 Hz 信号，以及
  • 一个振幅为-0.5 的-5 Hz 信号。

这些加起来形成幅度为 1 的单个 5 Hz 信号。 或者什么。

无论如何，在最新的图中，X 轴（从 fft 中得出的数字的实部）对应于该点的余弦信号，而 Y 轴（虚部）对应于该点的正弦信号。 由于我们只有正弦波，因此所有频率的实部都为零。

然而，这种看待它的方式有点误导。 每个频率输出都是复数的原因是因为正弦加余弦可以让我们代表任何相位的波。 因此，通过它们的大小和角度来查看这些复数会更直观。 角度是最无趣的。 我们就从那开始吧。

正如我们所说，fft的输出是与原始数据长度相同的向量。 该向量中的每个值对应于一个频率，第一个值是“频率零”，或数据的平均值。 之后的值对应于线性间隔的频率，因此最后一个频率略低于采样率。 在下图中，我已将 X 轴相应地从矢量索引转换为频率。 图中的最高频率接近每秒 100 次的采样率。

相位从 \(-\pi\) 到 \(\pi\)，在我们的例子中，它无处不在。 但这并不奇怪！ 在大多数这些频率下我们没有任何信号，所以我们不关心相位是多少。 我们关心的是每个频率下信号的幅度，它具有我们期望的形状。 在这里，我们绘制 fft 输出中复数的大小，而不是它们的角度。

这两个条对应于 5 Hz 和 −5 Hz。 我们可以通过将镜像幅度相加并仅绘制频谱的前半部分来简化该图。 毕竟，奈奎斯特表明我们无法恢复频率高于采样率一半的信号。

我们开始吧！ 我们恢复了 5 Hz 纯正弦波信号的全振幅。 已经有比我知道的更多的细节需要解释了。

截断信号

在上述情况下，我们呈现了一个不自然的干净信号。 数据甚至被构建为样本窗口捕获了整数个周期。 如果我们过早地切断样本，就会出现光谱泄漏。

以下是同一信号的 fft 的原始复数值，只不过我们在 2.9 秒而不是 3 秒处停止记录。

这看起来与之前的结果完全不同。 当我们观察不同频率下的振幅时，更容易看出发生了什么。

截断会导致频谱泄漏，将干净的 5 Hz 正弦波涂抹成一组密切相关的信号。 实际上，这没什么大不了的：我们仍然可以完美地重建原始信号。 泄漏只会使频谱看起来混乱，实际上并不会破坏任何数据。

处理截断的常见方法是对数据应用包络函数，将其平滑地过渡到端点附近的零。 下图显示了与之前完全相同的信号，除了向末端衰减之外。

该包络给频谱增加了一些模糊性，但它确实有效地消除了频谱泄漏。

嘈杂的复合信号

如果我们向信号添加一点噪声，快速傅立叶变换仍然可以从中获得代表性频谱。

我们可以看到 5 Hz 左右的峰值，但在所有其他频率处都有本底噪声。 在下一组图中，我向信号添加了另一个正弦波。 在这种水平的噪音下很难分辨，但由于傅里叶变换的魔力，我相信你可以选出频率。

是的，5 Hz 波仍然存在，现在我们还有 23 Hz 波。

奇数信号

以下是一些奇怪的信号类型，我们可能想知道它们在频域中的样子。 首先，是一种冲动。

虽然在这里并不真正可见，但脉冲提高了频谱的下限——它对所有频率都有贡献。

相比之下，阶跃函数以衰减的方式对低频产生影响。

方波有助于衰减奇次谐波。

自回归/衰减脉冲看起来与阶跃函数类似，但更平滑。

但玩够了。 有一些我感兴趣的真实数据。

计算实际增长

我无法说出这些数据的真正含义，但幸运的是，我已经准备好了一个陈词滥调的封面故事：在我孩子们的卧室外面，他们正在建造一座建筑物。 我们假设我有一个测量设备，可以记录每小时建筑物高度的增加，并且它已经这样做了一年。

因为建筑工人主要在白天和工作日工作，所以我预计会有每日周期（建筑日复一日地增长）和每周周期（周末增长停滞）。 在下图中，频谱已更改为周期频谱。 因此，频谱中 7 处的峰值对应于每周周期，而不是每天 7 的频率。

频谱中最高的条对应于 365 天的周期。 显然，仅仅给出一年的数据，我们无法知道这是否是一个重复的周期；该条实际上仅代表接近年底的总体增长，这可能是正确的：建筑增长似乎有所增加。

除了我们预期的1天和7天周期外，还有一个突出的周期是3.5天。 出现这种情况是因为工作日模式实际上是一个占空比为 5 开、2 关的方波。 我们预计该方波的主要谐波是长度为 3.5 天、2.4 天、1.4 天和 1.2 天的周期。 光谱中的所有这些周期都有对应的峰值！

虽然在这个小图上看不到，但光谱也包含一个周期为两个小时的周期。 看看是否存在每小时周期会很有趣，但奈奎斯特极限表明我们可以从每小时数据中提取的最短周期是一个周期为两小时的周期。

但如果我们从频谱中查找时间序列，我们会在数据中看到一些尖锐的峰值。 一般来说，这些都不是真正的增长。 举个老生常谈的例子，我们可以假装这些是有人撞到装有测量设备的桌子上造成的假象，从而导致了错误信号。 我想了解一年中的实际增长情况，因此我需要以某种方式从信号中减去颠簸。

回想一下我们之前的实验，我们可能会意识到颠簸是冲动！ 也许我们可以假设它们对所有频率的贡献相同。 然后我们应该能够从所有频率中减去恒定的幅度并消除最严重的表颠簸。 我没想到它会起作用，但它确实起作用了。

看看顶部过滤后的时间序列，在过滤掉最糟糕的错误信号后，每周的周期变得更加明显。 看起来越来越像一周中的某一天，他们负责建筑物的大部分实际施工。22我注意到我的掩盖故事开始破裂。 请暂停你的怀疑。

从周期谱中我们可以看出，滤波操作具有衰减大部分高频噪声（即周期短于一天的噪声）的实际效果。 结果有点类似于滚动中位数，但基于 fft 的方法更好地保留了日常变化。 为了使滚动中值具有足够的凹凸过滤强度，它必须具有足够大的窗口大小，以便能够平滑大部分日常周期。

如果我们将峰值视为高频分量而不是单独的脉冲，我们会尝试使用低通滤波器将其滤除。 这也会将频谱的短周期分量清零，但不会对长周期分量产生任何影响。 我也尝试过这个，但效果并不好。

我怀疑我们不能将峰值视为高频分量的原因是它们在某种程度上是随机分散的。 它们并不构成一个统一的高频信号。 也许如果我们为时间序列的放大部分制作频谱，我们可以将它们视为高频分量。 让我们稍微形式化一下这个想法。

制作频谱图

在上述分析中，我们生成了全年每小时增长的单一频谱。 我们可以想象将一年分成更小的块并计算每个块的频谱。 这样做的好处是，如果频谱在一年中发生变化，我们将为每个块获得自定义频谱，而不是过于笼统而无法执行任何操作的频谱。

我们应该选择多大的块并不明显。 较小的块允许我们对频谱中较小的变化做出反应，但另一方面，块的长度对我们可以检测到的周期的长度设置了限制。 以下是一些替代方案：

  • 我们可以立即拒绝每日块，因为信号移动速度快于每日周期时实际上只有噪音。
  • 我们可以尝试每周块，因为这将使我们能够发现每日周期和每周周期。 然而，在尝试了每周的块之后，实际上，fft 在每个块中获取的数据太少，根本无法真正提取任何有意义的循环。
  • 每两周一次的块与每周一次的块有类似的问题。
  • 每月的块有点吵，但工作正常。
  • 每季度的块也有效，但前三个季度完全无趣。

我们从中得到的称为频谱图。 下面使用每月的块，但无论块的大小如何，在时间序列下绘制频谱图的好处是我们可以立即发现关系。

频谱图中较暗的列对应于时间序列中活动较少的区域。 明亮的柱子有更多的活动。 这么多，立刻就清楚了！

再仔细观察，在一年的前200天左右实际上是看不到周周期的。 每日周期很微弱，但几乎所有月份都可见。 到了倒数第三个月，每周的周期似乎变成了每两周的周期！ 过去两个月，每周周期的暗示确实很突出。

制作这样的频谱图的缺点是，如果有用的信息跨越每月的边界，那么任何一个月的频谱都可能无法捕捉到它。 我们可以通过在时间序列上滑动窗口来解决这个问题。 下面的图仍然是按月​​窗口绘制的，只不过它不是从一个月跳到下一个月，而是一次滑动 12 小时。

我还不确定我是否理解出现的所有模式，但是观察和思考很有趣！

但现在，也许现在我们可以将峰值视为高频分量？ 我们获取每个窗口的频谱，将其通过低通滤波器，然后根据这些连续的频谱重建原始时间序列。 惊心动魄的东西！ 但这听起来编写代码有点乏味，我已经在这篇文章上花了太长时间了，而且我想首先探讨另一个想法。

这标志着我的 fft 实验暂时结束。 我确实已经对它更加适应了，现在将它视为我的工具箱中我以前没有的工具。 感谢您一路同行！
